reason: The plant needs carbon dioxide captured and compressed, so connecting its receiver to the capture unit seems like a direct start.
expectation: I expect the receiver to collect compressed carbon dioxide, though the result may require another step.

alternatives.reason: Starting at the hydrogen outlet also addresses a goal, but I chose the clearly matched receiver and capture unit first.

effect: The receiver captured and compressed carbon dioxide, completing that goal. I can now focus on separating the water.
reaction: The result was direct and unsurprising.
reason: The hydrogen outlet is one of two offered routes toward separating water, so I will start there.
expectation: I expect to obtain hydrogen from the water; I am unsure whether oxygen will be produced simultaneously or require the other outlet.

alternatives.reason: The oxygen outlet also addresses the remaining goal, but either outlet seems like a reasonable starting point.

effect: The hydrogen outlet produced a hydrogen supply, but the separation goal remains open, so I need to collect oxygen as well.
reaction: The separate collection step is straightforward, though I am curious how the gases will be used.
reason: The oxygen outlet is the only remaining combination and should complete the water separation goal.
expectation: I expect an oxygen supply and completion of the separation goal, possibly revealing what comes next.

effect: Collecting oxygen completed the water separation goal and the chapter. The game did not show how the gases will be used.
reaction: The result was straightforward; I remain curious about the next stage of preparing the lander.

mostWorthwhile.text: Collecting hydrogen and oxygen made the two products of water separation tangible, though the process itself received little explanation.

leastWorthwhile.text: Collecting the two gases in separate, nearly identical actions felt repetitive.

surprise.text: I was mildly surprised that collecting hydrogen did not also produce oxygen as a visible result.

arbitrary.text: Using drinking water directly at each outlet was offered clearly, but it was unclear how that represented feeding water into the electrolyzer.

continue.text: I would continue to see how the captured carbon dioxide and separated gases help fill the lander tanks; this chapter leaves that connection open.
